summary: Intermittent 429s after customer-side proxy rewrites auth header in Private VPC
description: Issue summary: Customer on a Redwood Private VPC deployment reports intermittent 429 throttles for regular production traffic after they rolled a change to their in-cluster Nginx proxy that rewrites authorization headers.
impact: Several customer applications experience intermittent request failures (429) during normal throughput peaks. Errors started approximately 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC after a proxy config change; customer reports 5-10% of requests getting 429s for a 2–4 minute window every ~15–30 minutes. Business impact: degraded ingestion and realtime features for customer-facing dashboards.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer change: Nginx sidecar configured to rewrite Authorization -> X-Custom-Auth for downstream logging (example config shown below).
2) Traffic pattern: many short-lived connections from a scheduler/fanout worker creating concurrent upstream connections (bursty).

3) Reproduce (internal): curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' https://edge.private.bluewave.example/api/v1/generate -> inspect edge logs, observe two auth headers forwarded (Authorization + X-Custom-Auth).

4) Observe: Control plane token-accounting increments twice for same logical request in environment where edge treats the rewritten header as a distinct credential source (race under connection reuse / keepalive).
5) Trigger: high churn of connections or worker restarts increases probability; HTTP/2 multiplexing of downstream clients also observed to change behavior.
Customer provided Nginx snippet: proxy_set_header X-Custom-Auth $http_authorization; proxy_hide_header Authorization; (they intended to hide original but misordered directives).
logs: 2026-03-09T22:03:12Z edge[auth-accounting] INFO request_id=abc123 tenant=bluewave token_source=Authorization increment=1 path=/api/v1/generate
2026-03-09T22:03:12Z edge[auth-accounting] INFO request_id=abc123 tenant=bluewave token_source=X-Custom-Auth increment=1 path=/api/v1/generate
Sample client trace (customer): 429 response returned with headers: x-rw-rate=tenant=bluewave;window=60;used=600;limit=600
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: double-counting of tokens due to both original and rewritten headers being visible to edge/accounting layers.

Reproduced in staging using a private VPC replica and an Nginx config that forwards both Authorization and an X- header: control-plane accounting recorded two token increments for a single logical caller when connection reuse/rewrite sequence aligned.

Observed higher likelihood when (a) keepalive connections are reused and Nginx worker reload happens, and (b) client uses HTTP/2 multiplexing which can interleave header frames across streams leading to transient header duplication in our edge adaptor.

Billing/Quota effect: tenant token counters hit short-window limits causing 429; counters are accurate to sources seen, but the same secret was being presented via two header names and treated as separate credential events.

Edge config check: our edge has a legacy header-normalization path that prefers 'Authorization' but will accept alternative header names for backward compatibility; in private installs that behavior was not explicitly documented and customer proxy alterations exposed the ambiguity.
Temporary mitigation tested: add an ingress rule to drop X-Custom-Auth at the edge; immediate disappearance of duplicate increment events in logs and 429s stopped in repro run.
customer_comments: 2026-03-10 - Customer (Ishaan Patel): We rolled a logging-related change to Nginx to surface auth in internal logs. After the change we saw spikes of 429s correlated with worker restarts. Disabling the rewrite removes the 429s immediately.

2026-03-10 - Support (Natalie Kim): Can you share the exact Nginx snippets and whether you use any HTTP/2 or connection pooling between services? Also asked for a short window of pcap/headers from a failing request.
2026-03-11 - Customer: Provided config and confirmed they use HTTP/2 between their ingress and sidecar; they also have a scheduled rolling deploy that coincides with the observed windows.
support_comments: 2026-03-10 - Omar Singh (SRE): Able to reproduce in staging. Created a temporary ingress rule to ignore X-Custom-Auth header for BlueWave namespace which mitigated the issue. Will propose a permanent control-plane dedupe for header-based auth sources.

2026-03-11 - Engineering: Patch created to prefer Authorization header and drop duplicated credential headers before token-accounting. PR linked in related_github_prs. Preparing staged rollout to private clusters.
2026-03-12 - Support: Requested customer to schedule a maintenance window to deploy the patch and apply temporary nginx ordering fixes (ensure proxy_pass does not expose both headers).
root_cause: Customer-side proxy rewrite produced a secondary auth header (X-Custom-Auth) while the original Authorization header remained visible in some request traces due to misordered proxy directives and connection reuse. The edge/control-plane historically accepted multiple header sources and counted credential appearances separately, producing duplicate accounting events that exhausted short-window token limits and triggered 429s.
resolution_summary: Deployed control-plane fix that deduplicates header-sourced credentials: if an Authorization header and an alternate auth header map to the same token value within a single request window, only one accounting increment is performed. Also deployed an ingress rule for the affected private cluster to ignore X-Custom-Auth while customer updates their Nginx configuration.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12 - Hotfix rolled to private-control-plane for BlueWave - dedupe logic enabled (canary 20% -> 100% over 2 hours).
Temporary edge ingress rule added to drop X-Custom-Auth for bluewave namespace (immediate mitigation).
Customer applied Nginx config change: reordered proxy_hide_header Authorization before proxy_set_header X-Custom-Auth and added a small TTL on keepalive to reduce window for misordering effects.
Monitoring: Added a short-term alert that watches for duplicate token-accounting events per request_id in private clusters.

Follow-ups: Update Private VPC runbook to call out header-rewrite anti-patterns; publish guidance for customers who must instrument auth headers for logging (recommend using internal logging pipelines rather than header rewrites).
next_steps: 1) Schedule post-mortem with BlueWave and internal SRE on 2026-03-18 to capture lessons and update runbooks.
2) Merge and backport the dedupe change to stable control-plane branches used by private deployments.
3) Document recommended Nginx/ALB patterns for Private customers in the Private VPC docs page.
4) Consider adding a configuration knob in private control-plane to ignore configured header names for quota-accounting on a per-tenant basis.
5) Close ticket after customer verifies behaviour for 48 hours post-fix.
